want.who_she_is: Rilla Vance, 27, nee Marek. Eleven weeks married to Dorn Vance, 54, who owns Vance Diesel — a repair yard on a county road outside Kerr Crossing, house on the same gravel lot. A paper signed before the wedding: nothing is hers for three years. No car in her name, not on the account, sixty dollars a week on the kitchen counter. Dorn put her on the books, so she writes down every number the yard makes and can touch none of them, and hands the week's cash to his eldest son on Friday. Dorn hauls four nights out of seven. What she has to lose: the three years, and the job she got her brother.
want.appetite: To be wanted by men who have to call her by a title she did not earn. It cannot complete — no figure of respect settles it, and every man who starts using her name has to be replaced by one still using the title. The yard supplies them: drivers, hires, family home from somewhere. Release 41 adds a new hire in the bunk room, a customer who becomes a regular, or another Vance who needs a bed.
want.ascent: Bottom: the office counter and the front rooms of the house, in daylight, with Dorn's name doing all the work; she asks Cade for the truck to leave the property at all. Top: the shop floor after close, the bunk room over it, the wash bay at midnight, the sleepers in the back row — and none of it needing his name, because by then they are not calling her by it. The ladders live on the cast: five men, two meters each (access — what he lets her near; willingness — how far he goes).

promises.text: Dorn's own ladder. He carries `want` with two rungs and zero gate sites — he is the week's clock in v0.1 and not yet a surface. Pay it or cut it.

Media. Every explicit surface declares `pool_dir` + `pool` and a search vocabulary; nothing is on disk. The real inventory, walked over every file-shaped string in the TOML: 22 FIXED references, all missing — 14 `locations[].image`, 6 `npcs[].portrait`, 2 `blocks[].props.file` — plus 34 distinct `pool_dir` directories, none of which exist. (This read "six external files" until 2026-08-25; six is the PACKAGER's warning and it counts portraits only, so the 14 location plates and 2 scene stills were invisible to the promise meant to track them. REVIEW.md L1.) find-media's job, not this skill's.
First visits for the nine locations that have none. The anchor introduces itself; the Back Row, the Bunk Room and the Bar carry the most prose without one.
The fill gap: v0.1 ships 10,297 words against a finished-world plan of 16,000 (`fill_finished`). Every release until it closes adds words to existing rooms, not rooms.
Dispatch depth: act_sleep, buy_propane and buy_drink each dispatch ONE outcome. Three to five per host is the shape.

The wardrobe is off (`clothing_enabled = false`). Arm it in the release that authors both a catalog and the beat that teaches it — a live system with nothing in it is a broken link in the home base on turn one.

The top half of four ladders. `board.cast_meters.rungs` declares the full climb and v0.1 builds the lower part of it: cade 82 declared / 42 built, booth 74 / 50, isaac 66 / 38, sherrod 62 / 34. Only tobin (70 / 70) reaches its own top. npc_dorn's second rung at 55 is now read by nothing at all — the quest cards that carried it were rebuilt on a played-flag in the Q1 repair. Deferring the upper half is correct for a release stream; leaving it unwritten was the defect (the-release.md:107, "log every promise and pay or cut it"). Pay it or cut the rungs. REVIEW.md L3.

`standing` is written 25 times across 23 canvases and READ four times, all four inside `work_counter` — a correctly-banded three-tier ladder that works, and the game's only customer for the meter. WANT.md §3 says it is "read constantly" and names three examples: the counter (built), the bank clerk's tone (zero reads in `the_bank`) and what the bar already knows (zero reads in `the_bar`). Field figure for comparison: reputation is read at 644 sites across the corpus. Adding reads to rooms that already exist is exactly what the fill promise describes; this names the first two. REVIEW.md S1/S2.

decisions.note: who_climbs = cast, decided before any meter was named (the-meters.md W1). All five prior v2 games measured 19-29% cast-gating, a band no shipped field game occupies, because the question was never asked. Cost: a roster game is more expensive to author than a ladder game.

Added npc_tobin (her brother) to the approved pitch, which was step-family only. Carries blood, gives the Vances someone to be jealous of, and inverts the roster's axis — the others climb toward taking her, he climbs toward being the one who never had to call her ma'am.

Locale locked to American-neutral at the Want rather than at the gate. Five v2 games shipped locale-locked nouns at 9.4-95.6 per 10,000 words against a field rate of 0.8, inherited from this skill's own worked examples. Cut list: forecourt, apron, frontage, tyre, lorry.

ascent_tiers = [] deliberately. 15 of 27 field sandboxes carry no player ascent tier and state.md calls an empty list legitimate for a cast game. Verified in gates.py: _school_split counts the player side as ONLY what ascent_tiers names, so this is a clean roster declaration rather than a dodge.

W6 as rewritten 2026-08-24 overrode the plan. The plan said two meters per man; the field gives every person exactly one meter and the SAME word (9 of 13 games), median 1 meter per person, and reserves the rich pair for the one or two arcs that carry the game. Shipping `want` on all six and `trust` on Cade and Booth only.

Needs are gated with `gte` (clean >= 40 to stand the counter), never `lt`. Gate 10's anti-narrowing descent test walks EVERY player trait and fails a meter whose lt reads outnumber its gte reads - a need written as a lock would read as a descent.

engine.md 30.1 argues against building a hygiene meter at all. Taking the M8 exception instead: `clean` drops on shop work AND on sex acts, has two restores at different prices, shuts two named doors, and routes her into the wash bay - which is a heat surface with no door. The failure 30.1 names is a decay hook nothing reads; this one is read.

Money carries clamp = false on every effect (engine.md 21). The engine clamps 0-100 by default, and a shipped game capped money at 100 against a 120 rent, making eviction the only reachable outcome. Obligation is 260, so this is not optional. Note the residual: a `costs` deduction is hard-clamped and truncates a balance above 100 (engine.md 27) - keep priced rungs cheap and the balance low, or she loses money on a purchase.

Re-planned board.locations[].fill from the finished-world budget (16,000) to a v0.1 seed budget (11400), in round numbers, and kept the original per-location figure as `fill_finished`. This is an amendment, not a back-fill: the numbers stay round, delivered does not equal declared anywhere, and the anchor is still sized against the FINISHED total (the_office 4,500 of 16,000 = 28%) rather than against what happens to be written today. Cost: v0.1 ships a world roughly two thirds the planned depth, and every release until it closes that gap adds words to existing rooms rather than rooms.

TWO SCHEMA REQUIREMENTS THE SKILL'S REFERENCES DO NOT CARRY, both found by the build refusing and neither documented in engine.md: (1) every [[canvases.nodes]] needs a `name`; (2) every [[quest_cards]] needs a `when`, INCLUDING a story-goal card. the-first-hour.md F8 says story cards are 'never gated this way' and the importer rejects one with no `when` — both are true at once, so the story cards carry a `when` on a flag the boot sets, live from click one.

Canvas `priority` is read off the TRIGGER (template_import.py:1914, trig_def.get('priority')), never off the canvas. Every priority in this game was written at canvas level first and was being silently discarded to 0 — valid TOML, green build, no warning. Same failure family as `op = "subtract"`.

Gate 26 walks the ROUTE INTO a canvas, not the price on the choice inside it. A located repeatable is entered by walking in, so `costs` on its choices brakes nothing — the brake has to be `max_triggers_per_day` or `costs` on the TRIGGER. This is the-economy R5's struck exemption in a new coat, and it caught act_wash_bay, the four purchase surfaces, every loop entry and every random event.

Live-verified the day-specific overnight split. Dorn's your_room window is [4,5,6] 22:30-23:59 plus [5,6,0] 00:00-05:30; probed at Saturday 01:00 he is present. As ONE row he would have been deleted at midnight, because the weekday check runs first and against today. The all-days rows (Isaac, Tobin, Sherrod, Booth) are correctly one row each and were probed present at Tuesday 00:15.

The arousal-gated FINISH link appeared to be missing from every act menu under a live probe. It was the moment-commit trap (engine.md §24 class): variables set from outside a passage transition are discarded by Engine.play. With setup.commitMoment() every menu renders its full ladder. Recorded because it is indistinguishable from a real defect and cost a probe to rule out.

0.1 was reviewed after shipping (games/mrs_vance/REVIEW.md, 21 items) and repaired in place rather than in a 0.1.1, because output/ is still the --dev --debug test artefact and nothing is published (`dev: true`, no `version`, REVIEW.md B1/N7). Fixed so far: P1 the ambient presence gate, Q1/Q2 the terminal badge moved off a meter onto a played-flag, C1/C2 the sleep label's clock, D1 the in-loop refusal text plus ten dead cooldown lines, T1 loop_solo's shared `loop_act`. Each carried its skill fix in the same commit. The release-time procedure is unchanged and lives on the portal entry (games-data.js:44-49).

`player.loop_act` is ONE trait shared by all six loops rather than one per loop. Kept shared — the five NPC loops each set it at entry and clear it on the finish exit, so the bands read only what the live loop wrote. `loop_solo` was the hole: it set `loop_stage` and never `loop_act`, which is safe only while its finisher has no bands, and adding bands there is exactly what the review's §4 asks for. Now sets 1 at entry and 0 on finish like the other five. REVIEW.md T1.

colour_meter.shape: W5b audience meter - it RISES and it almost never refuses
colour_meter.what: how much of the Vance name is actually hers. Rises when a man treats her as his father's wife in front of someone; falls when he treats her as something else in front of someone.
colour_meter.note: Read constantly to swap ONE line - the driver at the counter who talks to her or asks for a man, the clerk's tone, what the bar already knows. Field reads reputation at 644 sites and REFUSES at 2% of them. Do NOT apply W5's shuts-a-door test to this; W5 owns the meter that closes, W5b owns the meter that talks.

locations.job: The ground the whole world sits on - gravel between the house and the shop, opening onto the county road. Where anyone can see anything.
She keeps the books here because Dorn told her to. Cade signs, drivers come to the counter, and it sits between the house and the shop - the one room both worlds touch.
Four bays and a parts wall. Where the work is and where the men are all day.
Concrete, a drain, a hose on a reel, and no door. Where trucks get washed and where she gets clean when the house is full.
Over the shop. Two beds, a window on the yard. Isaac lives here and so does her brother.
Where overnight trucks park, each with a bed behind the seats. The far end of the property and the last place anybody looks.
Up the outside stairs over the office. He has been here longer than the marriage and he has never said what he thinks he is owed.
The back door of the house opens into it. Where the family is a family, three nights a week.
Hers and Dorn's, and his four nights of the week. Where the day ends.
One bathroom, five adults, a bolt that does not sit in its keeper.
The youngest one's room, and the only one in the house who still means the title.
The crossroads twenty minutes down the road. Pumps, a light, and the only place on earth nobody here owns.
Where the account she is not on lives.
The one room in the world where nobody calls her Mrs. Vance, and the men from the yard drink here too.
